title: EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA SIMPLEX 7, WITH NEPHROPATHY AND DEAFNESS
alt_titles: NEPHROPATHY WITH PRETIBIAL EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA AND DEAFNESS

relationships.phenotype: EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA SIMPLEX 7, WITH NEPHROPATHY AND DEAFNESS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that epidermolysis bullosa simplex with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CD151 gene (602243) on chromosome 11p15.5.

checks.claim: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CD151 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: The 3 patients are homozygous for a single nucleotide insertion (G383) in exon 5 of CD151, causing a frameshift and premature stop signal at codon 140.
checks.explanation: The paper reports a homozygous CD151 mutation in the patients, but the abstract never uses the disorder name 'EBS7'. Only the 2 sibs had the skin and deafness features; the third patient is described with kidney disease only.

checks.claim: The CD151 gene is located on chromosome 11p15.5.
checks.evidence_quote: It is encoded by a gene at the same position on chromosome 11p15.5 as the MER2 blood group gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this location directly.

paragraphs.text: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex with nephropathy and deafness is characterized by pretibial blistering of the skin (pretibial epidermolysis bullosa), hereditary nephritis that progresses to end-stage kidney disease, and sensorineural deafness (Karamatic Crew et al., 2004). CD151 expresses the MER2 blood group antigen, and affected individuals are MER2-negative. Affected individuals are homozygous for a CD151 mutation predicted to produce a truncated protein that would lack its integrin-binding domain (Karamatic Crew et al., 2004).

paragraphs.text: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) studied 3 MER2-negative patients from 2 families, 2 of whom were sibs. All 3 had end-stage kidney disease due to hereditary nephritis. The sibs also had sensorineural deafness and pretibial epidermolysis bullosa.

paragraphs.text: In 3 MER2-negative patients with hereditary nephritis, 2 of whom were sibs who also had pretibial epidermolysis bullosa and deafness, Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) identified a homozygous single-nucleotide insertion in the CD151 gene that caused a frameshift. The resulting truncated protein would lack its integrin-binding domain. The authors concluded that CD151 is essential for the proper assembly of the glomerular and tubular basement membrane in the kidney, has functional significance in the skin, and is probably a component of the inner ear.
